absent: Full memblock type and region structure layout beyond the fields touched by insertion and search.
Free-range iterator guarantees, node and flag filtering semantics, and bottom-up counterpart behavior.
Slab state enumeration values and transition events that reach UP.
Deferred page-map initialization condition and its interaction with freeing.
Per-CPU lock ordering, interrupt context rules, and chunk list slot sizing beyond creation accounting.
Remainder of pcpu_build_alloc_info after group map fill, including final padding and error paths.
Numeric values of page size, cache line size, bitmap block size, minimum allocation and unit sizes, and early dynamic reserve.
Runtime per-CPU allocation, free, population, and reclaim paths beyond first-chunk setup.

findings.text: Boot-time initialization entry that consumes a caller-supplied allocation description plus a base address and publishes the first per-CPU chunks and global addressing tables. It validates inputs, builds per-group and per-CPU maps, allocates chunk list slots, splits the first chunk into static plus reserved plus dynamic portions, and records the base address on success.
Availability query that reports whether the slab subsystem has progressed at least to its UP state. Callers use it as a gate before attempting slab allocation.

Top-down free-range search scans free memory ranges in reverse, constrains each candidate range to the requested start and end bounds, skips ranges whose constrained end is smaller than the requested size, otherwise rounds the end-minus-size result down to the requested alignment and returns the first candidate at or above the constrained start; failure returns zero.

Ordered region insertion at a caller-chosen index asserts capacity remains, shifts later descriptors up by one slot, stores base and size plus flags and node identity, then increments the region count and adds the size to the total. The caller owns index choice and ordering.

Reserved-area release refuses to proceed when deferred page-map initialization is active, warning and returning zero. Otherwise it walks every valid page frame in the half-open frame interval derived from the byte range, obtains a writable direct-map address through the page structure, clears address tagging, optionally fills the page when the poison value fits in a byte, frees the page as reserved, and returns the count freed.
Allocation-description teardown releases the descriptor with the early reservation allocator using the size recorded inside the descriptor itself.

First-chunk setup validates every sizing and alignment precondition with a fatal diagnostic helper that logs the failed predicate and the possible-CPU mask, dumps the allocation description, and halts. Checked properties include group count, base presence and page alignment, unit size covering the summed regions and meeting minimum and bitmap granularity, dynamic and reserved sizing and alignment, page versus bitmap block compatibility, and backend verification success.

Setup builds flat per-group offset and size tables and per-CPU unit index and offset tables, initializes all CPU mappings to an invalid sentinel, then assigns each described CPU a monotonically increasing unit number and a byte offset from its group base plus unit stride, tracking the CPUs with lowest and highest offsets and rejecting duplicates, out-of-range or impossible CPUs and any possible CPU left unmapped.

Setup derives unit page count and byte size, atom size and chunk header size, allocates and initializes a consecutive run of chunk lists with three trailing special slots for sidelined plus fully free plus to-depopulate chunks, aligns the static prefix up to minimum allocation granularity while shrinking the dynamic portion to compensate, creates optional reserved and mandatory dynamic first chunks at the corresponding offsets, relocates the dynamic chunk, accounts populated pages for the summed size, emits creation trace and statistics, and publishes the base address.

Statistics helpers exist in two build variants: an active variant that snapshots the allocation description and seeds the minimum allocation size from the unit size and that counts chunk creation with peak tracking, and an inert variant that performs no action.
Active chunk-creation accounting serializes counter and peak updates under the per-CPU subsystem spinlock with interrupt state saved and restored.

Backend verification policy differs: one backend accepts only a single group and otherwise reports an invalid-argument failure, computes total versus power-of-two-rounded page counts and warns about per-chunk waste; the other backend imposes no additional restriction and always reports success.

First-chunk construction page-aligns the supplied address down, derives the leading offset and the page-rounded span covering offset plus mapped size, allocates the chunk header sized for its page-population bitmap plus allocation and boundary bitmaps plus per-block metadata, initializes list linkage and base and edge offsets and page count, initializes block metadata, marks the chunk immutable and fully populated with all pages initially empty, sets free bytes to the mapped size, and hides any leading or trailing partial granules in the bitmaps while updating allocation hints.
The number of bitmap blocks in a chunk equals total chunk bytes divided by the bitmap block byte size.

Allocation hint maintenance translates the allocated bit interval into start and end block indexes with half-open intra-block offsets, refreshes first-free and scan and contiguous hints plus left and right edge free counts for affected endpoint blocks with rescans when overlap breaks an existing hint, clears hints on fully covered interior blocks, decrements the empty-page estimate for blocks transitioning away from fully free, and clears or refreshes chunk-level scan and contiguous hints on overlap.
Interval overlap test treats both inputs as half-open ranges and reports true exactly when each start precedes the other end.

Block hint refresh promotes any pending scan hint into the contiguous hint and resumes scanning after it, otherwise restarts from the first free position with an empty contiguous hint, clears the trailing free count, then folds every free bit run into the block contiguity summary.

Metadata initialization seeds the chunk-wide summary with the full map bit count and seeds every per-block summary with the per-block bit count, using zero scan hint, full contiguous and edge free counts, zero first-free position, and the supplied bit capacity.

Diagnostic dump computes decimal widths for group and CPU numbers, units per allocation and allocations per log line, logs static plus reserved plus dynamic plus unit plus atom sizing, then logs each allocation group with its CPU mapping using placeholders for empty slots. It performs no state mutation beyond logging.

Allocation-description construction measures the static per-CPU image, page-aligns the sum of static plus reserved plus at least the early-dynamic minimum and derives the dynamic size as the remainder, then chooses a minimum unit size covering that sum or the architectural minimum and an atom-multiple allocation size with a page-aligned unit stride.

Construction groups possible CPUs by mutual locality according to an optional distance function with each ungrouped CPU seeding a new group, then selects the largest units-per-allocation value that preserves atom divisibility and page alignment, keeps total waste at or below one third of possible CPUs, and does not increase total allocation count, aborting if none qualifies; it then allocates the descriptor with per-group unit counts rounded up and fills sizes, strides, back-to-back base offsets, and CPU maps.

Allocation description carries static, reserved, dynamic, unit, atom and allocation sizes, group count, and an array of group descriptors each with base offset, unit count and CPU map; setup additionally builds parallel group offset and size arrays plus per-CPU unit index and byte-offset arrays and publishes group count, unit count, page count, sizes and low and high unit CPUs.

Chunk state observed includes list linkage, base address, leading and trailing offsets, page and population counts, empty-page estimate, free bytes, immutability flag, population bitmap, allocation and boundary bitmaps, per-block metadata array, and a chunk-wide summary; each block summary carries scan and contiguous hints with starts, left and right edge free counts, first-free position, and bit capacity.

Two lifecycle gates appear: slab availability is a monotonic state comparison against UP, and per-CPU first-chunk bring-up proceeds through validate inputs, build CPU and group tables, publish global geometry and allocate list slots, instantiate reserved then dynamic chunks, relocate and account population, then publish the base address.

Several misuses halt execution: inserting beyond region capacity, supplying inconsistent first-chunk geometry or unmapped or duplicated CPUs, or selecting no viable units-per-allocation. Releasing reserved pages while deferred map initialization is active warns and performs no release rather than halting.

Reserved-page release must use the writable direct-map alias derived via the page structure rather than assuming identity with the kernel virtual address, must strip address tagging before an unchecked fill, and must only fill when the poison operand fits in one byte.

Observed sizing rules state page granularity for base addresses and unit sizes and region spans, minimum unit and bitmap-block and minimum-allocation granularity for unit and reserved and static sizes, early-dynamic minimum for the dynamic region, cache-line granularity for early table allocations, and sentinel values for unmapped CPUs.
